notes: §1985:VI.6.18.3 SR10: 'The same character must not appear more than once either in literal-4 or in the data item referenced by identifier-6.' BindPhraseOperands calls CheckInspectConvertingRepeatedCharacter on the CONVERTING operand; below 2002 it scans a literal-4 and reports COBOL6859 at the first repeated character; identifier-6's content is a run-time value no syntax check can see, and from 2002 the rule is gone (first occurrence used). Probes at 85: (b) 'ABA', 'AA' TO SPACE, 'A  ' (space twice) and a 37-character literal-4 continued across a line with A repeated on the continuation are COBOL6859; 'ABCD' TO 'abcd' runs 'abcdabcd' and 'Aa' (case distinct) runs. (d/f) an identifier-6 and a FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(WS-2) holding 'AA' at run time compile and convert by the first occurrence ('XBCDXBCD'), outside what a syntax rule can check. (c) at --std 2002 'ABA' TO 'XYZ' compiles and runs 'XYCDXYCD'. The witness's CONVERTING 'ABA' TO 'XYZ' is COBOL6859.

next.reason: 1985: "The same character must not appear more than once either in literal-4 or in the data item referenced by identifier-6."; 2023: "If the same character appears more than once in ... identifier-6 or in literal-4, the first occurrence of the character is used for replacement.". 1985 forbids duplicate characters in literal-4/identifier-6. 2023 accepts such programs and defines the result: the first occurrence is used for replacement.
